# foldtoc

foldtoc writes a table of contents into your Markdown files. Any section that has sub-sections is folded behind a ▶ toggle, so a long document's TOC stays short: readers see the top-level sections and open only the parts they need.

It's a drop-in replacement for [doctoc](https://github.com/thlorenz/doctoc). The command works the same way, the main flags are the same, and it replaces existing doctoc TOCs in place. The table of contents below was generated by foldtoc, so you can click ▶ to try it.

## Quick start

1. Install foldtoc. It needs Node.js 18.3 or later.

   ```sh
   npm install --global foldtoc
   ```

2. Optional: choose where the TOC goes. By default it's added at the very top of the file. To put it somewhere else, such as below your title, paste these two lines there:

   ```md
   <!-- START foldtoc -->
   <!-- END foldtoc -->
   ```

3. Generate the TOC:

   ```sh
   foldtoc README.md    # one file
   foldtoc .            # every Markdown file under the current folder
   ```

Run the same command again whenever your headings change, and the TOC is updated in place. To try foldtoc without installing it, run `npx foldtoc README.md`. See [Usage](#usage) for more.

## What it generates

For a document with these headings:

```md
# Hashmap
## Create a hashmap
## Count frequencies
### Using a for loop
### Using a Counter
# Hashset
## Create a hashset
# Sorting
```

foldtoc writes this:

```md
**Table of Contents**

- <details><summary><a href="#hashmap">Hashmap</a></summary>

  - [Create a hashmap](#create-a-hashmap)
  - <details><summary><a href="#count-frequencies">Count frequencies</a></summary>

    - [Using a for loop](#using-a-for-loop)
    - [Using a Counter](#using-a-counter)
    </details>

  </details>

- <details><summary><a href="#hashset">Hashset</a></summary>

  - [Create a hashset](#create-a-hashset)
  </details>

- [Sorting](#sorting)
```

On GitHub this shows three lines: ▶ Hashmap, ▶ Hashset and Sorting. Clicking ▶ opens a section. Clicking a section's name jumps to it.

Two details:

- If the TOC has only one top-level entry, such as a README with a single `# Title`, that entry starts open. Otherwise the whole TOC would be hidden behind one toggle.
- Markdown isn't rendered inside `<summary>`, so foldtoc converts formatting in those headings to HTML. For example, `` `code` `` becomes `<code>code</code>`.

## Usage

### Choose files and folders

```sh
foldtoc README.md                  # a file in the current folder
foldtoc docs/guide.md              # a relative path
foldtoc /Users/me/notes/algo.md    # an absolute path
foldtoc .                          # every Markdown file under the current folder
foldtoc README.md docs             # any mix of files and folders
```

In a folder, foldtoc processes `.md`, `.markdown` and `.mdx` files in all subfolders. It skips `node_modules` and `.git`. A file you name directly is processed whatever its extension.

Running foldtoc again updates the TOC in place, so it's safe in a pre-commit hook or a watch script.

### Place the TOC

The first run puts the TOC at the top of the file, below any front matter. To put it somewhere else, add these two lines where you want it and run foldtoc:

```md
<!-- START foldtoc -->
<!-- END foldtoc -->
```

Everything between the two lines is replaced on each run. Only headings below the TOC are listed, so a title above it stays out. Use `--all` to list every heading.

### Leave things out

- Put `<!-- FOLDTOC SKIP -->` anywhere in a file to have foldtoc leave that file alone.
- Put `<!-- FOLDTOC EXCLUDE -->` on the line directly above a heading to drop that heading and its sub-sections from the TOC.

The doctoc spellings, `<!-- DOCTOC SKIP -->` and `<!-- DOCTOC EXCLUDE -->`, work too.

### Delete a section

Selecting a long section in an editor to delete it is tedious. `foldtoc rm` deletes whole sections for you, each with its heading, its text and all its sub-sections, and then updates the TOC:

```sh
foldtoc rm algo.md "#heap--priority-queue"      # by anchor, copied from the TOC
foldtoc rm algo.md "Heap / Priority Queue"      # or by heading text
foldtoc rm algo.md "#sorting" "#intervals"      # several at once
```

Before deleting anything, it shows what it will remove and asks for confirmation:

```text
About to delete from algo.md:
  # Heap / Priority Queue  (lines 49-58, 9 sub-sections)
Delete? [y/N]
```

- `-y` or `--yes` skips the question. You need it in scripts, where there's no terminal to ask on.
- Heading text is matched ignoring case and formatting. If several headings share a name, such as "Practice", foldtoc lists their anchors so you can pick one.
- A section runs up to the next heading of the same or a higher level.
- A section that contains the TOC can't be deleted.
- The TOC is rebuilt, not just trimmed, because deleting a section can change the anchors of later headings with the same name (`#practice-3` becomes `#practice-2`). If you usually run foldtoc with options such as `--title` or `--maxlevel`, pass them to `rm` too.

### Check in CI

```sh
npx foldtoc --dryrun .
```

With `--dryrun`, nothing is written. The exit code is 1 if any file's TOC is missing or out of date.

## Options

| Option | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `--title <markdown>` | Title above the TOC. Default: `**Table of Contents**` |
| `--notitle` | No title |
| `--minlevel <1-6>` | Shallowest heading level to include. Default: 1 |
| `--maxlevel <1-6>` | Deepest heading level to include. Default: 6 |
| `--all` | Also include headings above the TOC |
| `-u`, `--update-only` | Only update files that already have a TOC |
| `--entryprefix <char>` | List bullet: `-`, `*` or `+`. Default: `-` |
| `--github` | Anchors that match GitHub (default) |
| `--gitlab` | Anchors that match GitLab |
| `-s`, `--stdout` | Print the result instead of writing the file (one file only) |
| `--dryrun` | Write nothing; exit with 1 if any file is out of date |
| `--loglevel <level>` | `silent`, `error`, `warn`, `info`, `debug` or `trace`. Default: `info` |
| `-h`, `--help` | Show help |
| `-v`, `--version` | Show the version |

Exit codes: `0` means success. `1` means a file couldn't be processed or, with `--dryrun`, is out of date. `2` means the command line was invalid.

## Coming from doctoc

Replace `doctoc` with `foldtoc` in your command. The first run replaces doctoc's TOC where it is; both marker styles, `<!-- START doctoc generated TOC ... -->` and `<!-- START doctoc -->`, are recognized. From then on the file has foldtoc markers, so run foldtoc on it, not doctoc. Running doctoc would add a second TOC.

Differences:

- The default title is just `**Table of Contents**`, with no credit line.
- Only GitHub and GitLab anchors are supported. `--bitbucket` is refused because Bitbucket doesn't render HTML in Markdown, so the toggles can't work there. `--nodejs` and `--ghost` aren't supported.
- `--entryprefix` takes a single bullet. Different bullets per level aren't supported.
- These doctoc options aren't available and are rejected as unknown options: `--toc-location`, `--toc-pragma-style`, `--toc-header-content`, `--toc-footer-content`, `--toc-title-padding-before`, `--document-lines-min`, `--mintocitems`, `--toc-list-format`, `--toc-list-style`, `--toc-items-indentation-style` and `--toc-items-indentation-width`.

foldtoc is an independent project. It isn't affiliated with doctoc or its authors.
